outputs: Machine-generated texts (summaries from summarization systems and continuations from language models)
Coherence scores for pairwise ranking of generated texts
The paper addresses generated outputs in summarization and machine translation, evaluating their coherence using proposed models.

changes_made.explanation: Removed 'Dialogue Generation' as it's not evaluated in the paper. Normalized model names to standard forms. Removed redundant output description. Kept only NLG tasks explicitly evaluated.
Removed BLEU and ROUGE as they are only mentioned as examples of traditional metrics that are insufficient, not actually used for evaluation. The paper uses Accuracy for pairwise coherence ranking.
Cleaned up empty values. No LLM-as-judge evaluation is conducted in this paper.

guideline: Workers were instructed about the concept of coherence and shown examples of coherent and incoherent texts
Given the prompt, they were asked to choose the more coherent text out of two given language model outputs
Option to choose neither if texts were equally coherent/incoherent
Workers were instructed about the concept of coherence and shown examples of coherent and incoherent texts.
Annotators were asked to select the more coherent of two texts (or none if equally coherent), based on the definition and examples of coherence provided.

Workers were instructed about the concept of coherence and shown examples of coherent and incoherent texts. Given the prompt, they were asked to choose the more coherent text out of two given language model outputs; they were also given an option to choose neither in case the texts were equally coherent/incoherent.

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated multiple similar guideline descriptions into a concise version. Kept coherence as the only evaluation criterion.

overall_notes: The paper focuses on coherence modeling for evaluating NLG outputs. It evaluates coherence models on various NLG tasks but does not generate text itself. Human evaluation was conducted via Amazon Mechanical Turk for the LMVLM dataset. Automatic evaluation used accuracy for pairwise coherence ranking. No LLM-as-judge evaluation was conducted.
